title: Feelings and states
intro: Nearly everything here takes estar, not ser, because a feeling is a state and not an identity. The exception is ser + adjective for a lasting trait: es nervioso means he is a nervous sort, está nervioso means he is nervous right now.

entries.note: Plural felices. Used of a settled happiness; contento is the everyday word for pleased.

ex.es: Nunca la había visto tan feliz.
ex.en: I'd never seen her so happy.

entries.note: Always with estar. The commonest reply to ¿cómo estás?

ex.es: Se puso triste al leer la carta.
ex.en: He grew sad reading the letter.

entries.note: enojado in Latin America, enfadado in Spain. enojarse is to get angry.
You have fear rather than being afraid: tengo miedo. dar miedo is to frighten.

ex.es: Me pongo nervioso antes de hablar.

entries.note: ¡Tranquilo! on its own means take it easy.

ex.en: Don't worry, I've already fixed it.

entries.note: preocuparse por is to worry about.
enamorarse de is to fall in love with.
el odio is hatred. Strong — for milder dislike use no me gusta nada.
Built backwards: the thing liked is the subject. Me gusta el café is literally coffee pleases me. Plural things take gustan.
Works exactly like gustar but stronger: me encanta is I love it. Never me encanta mucho.
Usually reflexive with de: reírse de algo, to laugh at something. la risa is laughter.

ex.en: The baby cried until it fell asleep.

entries.note: la sonrisa is a smile. Same pattern as reír.
¡Buena suerte! is good luck. tener suerte is to be lucky.

ex.es: Tuvimos mucha suerte con el clima.
ex.en: We were very lucky with the weather.
He accepted his fate without complaining.

entries.note: dar vergüenza is to embarrass. Remember embarazada means pregnant, not embarrassed.

ex.es: Me da vergüenza preguntar otra vez.

entries.note: ¡Ánimo! is cheer up or you can do it.
extrañar in Latin America; echar de menos in Spain.

ex.en: I miss my family a lot.

ex.es: Me extraña que no haya llamado.
ex.en: I find it strange that he hasn't called.

entries.note: tener ganas de + infinitive is to feel like doing something. Almost always plural.

ex.es: No tengo ganas de salir hoy.
ex.en: I don't feel like going out today.
